source.title: Grokking as a Variance-Limited Phase Transition: Spectral Gating and the Epsilon-Stability Threshold

record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking on modular-addition tasks, an algorithmic generalization setting separate from the claim’s natural-label setting. It does not test any listed version on natural-label held-out data.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on modular addition, not natural labels. These related algorithmic-task results are recorded under versions ["none"]. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports modular-addition grokking, but does not test any specified version. It lacks random-label controls (V1), widening beyond verified interpolation (V2), the architectural, batch-size, dropout or removal comparisons (V3, V5, V6, V8), and the benchmark optimizer comparison specified by V4. Its unscaled Hessian sharpness versus an optimizer stability threshold does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its correlation with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. They propose that grokking depends on sufficient embedding capacity, task complexity, and a variance-dependent stability gate, and argue that adaptive anisotropic updates are necessary for complete generalization in their setup. Their experiments concern modular addition; the asserted necessity and uniqueness of adaptive rectification are stronger than the limited optimizer comparison establishes.
record.recipe_differences: Modular-addition grokking with a two-hidden-layer MLP, full-batch AdamW and isotropic SGLD comparisons; not the natural-label image or language settings in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Task modulus, optimizer stability ϵ, weight decay, isotropic versus adaptive noise, and embedding dimension change the reported outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Generalization delay peaks at intermediate modulus, disappears for high-modulus tasks, and some configurations fail when embedding capacity is insufficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this modular-addition MLP setup, grokking depends on task modulus, embedding capacity and optimizer stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher weight decay accelerates grokking, and intermediate tasks have an optimal AdamW epsilon region near 10^-4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay and AdamW epsilon affect the timing and attainment of modular-addition grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: The reported generalizing-basin Hessian curvature is 721.31 times the initial optimizer stability threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the P = 41 experiment, delayed generalization accompanies access to curvature exceeding the initial stability threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Isotropic SGLD maintains weight norm but fails to generalize in the main comparison; supplementary noise injection reaches approximately 60–80% accuracy without perfect generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Isotropic noise can aid optimization in these modular-addition experiments without reproducing AdamW's complete grokking transition.

record.problems: The experiments use one stated MLP setup on modular addition, which does not test the natural-label claim. Many result values are figure-only; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The SGLD comparison is reported for specified modular tasks and does not establish behavior on image or language benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper’s discussion of prior studies is not extracted as this study’s own result.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label training, near-perfect random-label fitting, and their held-out accuracy comparison.
Test error as hidden width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error, with training to convergence without explicit regularization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD or momentum SGD performance on image or language benchmarks under the specified tuning regimes and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and whether adapted training recipes remove their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out classifier error, including small-data, excessive-dropout and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps across comparably fitted convolutional networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus an equal number of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not deny the unrelated outcomes reported in the text. Exclusion rests on the missing defining comparisons and measures, not simply on the use of algorithmic data. The paper's argument against generic flat-minimum explanations does not directly challenge V7's specific correlational claim.

versions.untested_parts: Natural labels and random-label controls; the paper studies modular addition.
Width sweep beyond interpolation on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons on image-classification or language benchmarks.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons across networks with matched training loss.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Swept task modulus P and optimizer stability ϵ; measured steps to test accuracy > 99%.
rows.note: The text describes regimes and boundaries but gives no per-configuration values.
rows.check: Time to grok across modulus and epsilon does not measure a listed version. Render the training budget as 10^6 steps.

rows.operation_detail: Varied task modulus and measured generalization time.
rows.value: Figure only; gap peaks at P = 41
rows.note: The text says intermediate tasks exhibit the canonical grokking gap, peaking at P = 41.
rows.check: The reported maximum grokking delay concerns training dynamics, not any listed effect.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Varied task modulus and measured generalization time.
rows.value: The grokking delay vanishes; hard tasks generalize immediately
rows.note: Authors attribute this to Stability Override.
rows.check: Immediate generalization at high modulus does not test any listed comparison; the network width is fixed.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Increased weight decay and measured the phase transition.
rows.measure: Test accuracy versus steps / transition speed
rows.value: Figure only; higher weight decay significantly accelerates the phase transition
rows.note: The figure caption explicitly describes acceleration; a numeric accuracy or time is not given.
rows.check: Weight-decay effects on transition timing do not test dropout or the optimizer comparison specified by V4.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Varied optimizer stability parameter ϵ and measured phase-transition performance.
rows.baseline: Other ϵ settings; values figure only
rows.value: Figure only; convex optimal-stability region around ϵ = 10−4 for intermediate tasks
rows.note: No per-setting numerical values are stated.
rows.check: An optimal AdamW epsilon interval on modular addition does not measure any listed effect.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian sharpness with the initial stability limit during grokking.
rows.note: The authors state that the generalizing minimum is 721.31x higher in λmax than the initial stability threshold.
rows.check: The 721.31-fold ratio compares generalizing-basin Hessian curvature with the initial stability threshold, not magnitude-aware sharpness with generalization gaps. The 0–200k-step interval describes the preceding delay, not the condition at which this ratio is measured.

rows.subject: SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Injected isotropic Gaussian noise into standard SGD updates and compared with AdamW.
rows.value: Flatline at Random Chance; fails to generalize
rows.note: The result is for isotropic SGLD on the hard task; the caption states extensive noise tuning.
rows.check: SGLD failure on modular addition does not test V4's benchmark comparison. The subject is the MLP trained with SGLD, rather than SGLD as a separate system. Section 5.5 does not explicitly identify Figure 8's modulus; P = 67 should be marked as inferred. The budget is 10^6 steps.

rows.subject: SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Injected isotropic Gaussian noise and measured weight norm.
rows.note: The authors say isotropic noise maintains the weight norm despite not generalizing.
rows.check: Weight-norm stationarity is not a listed generalization effect. The subject is the MLP trained with SGLD. Figure 8's modulus is not explicitly identified in the supplied text; the budget is 10^6 steps.

rows.subject: SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Measured Fourier sparsity and Hessian trace during isotropic-noise training.
rows.baseline: AdamW characteristic ignition, as described by authors
rows.value: Fourier sparsity remains high; Hessian trace lacks the characteristic “Ignition” spike
rows.note: The paper reports structural stagnation under SGLD.
rows.check: Fourier sparsity and Hessian trace are distinct measures and should be separate rows. Neither measures V7. The subject is the MLP trained with SGLD; Figure 9's modulus is not explicitly identified in the supplied text.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Injected isotropic Gaussian noise and compared with the noiseless baseline.
rows.note: The text says noise outperforms the noiseless baseline but does not induce perfect generalization.
rows.check: The reported 60–80% accuracy under isotropic noise is supported, but does not measure any listed effect. Appendix A.4 does not supply individual modulus values or numerical baseline accuracies.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (width 128, ReLU activations)
rows.operation_detail: Ablated embedding dimension V against modulus P and measured time to grok.
rows.value: Failure when embedding dimension is insufficient relative to modulus (V ≲ P); Figure 10 shows configurations failing within 106 steps
rows.note: The text attributes failure to insufficient geometric capacity and rank-deficient gradient signal.
rows.check: Embedding capacity versus modulus is not V2's hidden-width sweep beyond zero training error. The text supplies neither verified interpolation nor a continuing decrease in test error. The evaluation budget is 10^6 steps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
